title: DC Fast-Charge Share vs Target
dataSources: Tesla vehicle and charge state (`tesla:vehicle`, `tesla:charge`), OBD-II PIDs (`obd:pid`), Smart EV charger sessions (`evcharger:session`).
app: Tesla Fleet API / TeslaMate, TeslaFi, and generic OBD-II / Smartcar / charger APIs via HEC scripted inputs and MQTT.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=evcharger:session
| bin _time span=1mon
| stats sum(eval(charge_type="dc_fast")) as dc_fast, count as total_sessions by vin _time
| eval fast_share=round(100*dc_fast/total_sessions,1)
| where total_sessions>=4 AND fast_share>40
| sort - fast_share
description: Calculates how much of your charging month is coming from expensive fast chargers instead of cheaper home or destination charging.
value: Fast charging is fantastic and usually costs more; keeping its share visible helps you budget and monitor battery-use patterns at the same time.
implementation: Capture charger session type and count; review monthly and compare fast-charge share against your own cost or battery-care target.
visualization: Monthly chart of DC fast-charge share.
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Splunk Enterprise ≥9.0 or Splunk Cloud — a single-instance home lab is fine. Create `index=personal` with 90–365 day retention (`indexes.conf`).
• **HEC token**: Settings → Data Inputs → HTTP Event Collector → New Token → index `personal`. Store the token in your connector's environment (never commit it to git).
• **Upstream product**: Personal HEC index — HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.
• **Subcategory context**: Connected Cars & EVs — typical feeds: Tesla vehicle/charge state (`tesla:vehicle`, `tesla:charge`), TeslaMate MQTT/Postgres, OBD-II PIDs (`obd:pid`), Smartcar API (`smartcar:vehicle`), EV charger sessions (`evcharger:session`)..
• **Sourcetypes in this search**: `evcharger:session`.
• **Network**: The connector host must reach both the vendor API/MQTT broker and your Splunk HEC port (8088/tcp).

## Step 1 — Configure data collection

Route **Personal HEC index** events into `index=personal` with `sourcetype=evcharger:session`.

**Collection method:** HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.

**Reference endpoint / path:** `POST https://<splunk>:8088/services/collector/event`.

**Suggested poll interval:** depends on upstream connector.

**Key fields to extract:** `sourcetype-specific — see search filters`.

**Typical connector stack:** Tesla Fleet API / TeslaMate, Teslafi, and generic OBD-II / Smartcar / manufacturer APIs via HEC scripted inputs and MQTT..

**Author notes:** Capture charger session type and count; review monthly and compare fast-charge share against your own cost or battery-care target.


Example HEC payload shape:

```json
{"index": "personal", "sourcetype": "evcharger:session", "event": { ... vendor fields ... }}
```

Verify ingestion with:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=evcharger:session earliest=-24h | head 20
```

## Step 2 — Create the search and alert

This search implements **DC Fast-Charge Share vs Target** over `personal` data (primarily `sourcetype=evcharger:session`) across the full search range. It applies numeric thresholds on `total_sessions` (>= 4) after sum — tune these constants to your household baseline.

**Fields this search depends on:** `_time`, `fast_share`, `total_sessions`, `vin`. Confirm each is populated before scheduling alerts.

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=evcharger:session
| bin _time span=1mon
| stats sum(eval(charge_type="dc_fast")) as dc_fast, count as total_sessions by vin _time
| eval fast_share=round(100*dc_fast/total_sessions,1)
| where total_sessions>=4 AND fast_share>40
| sort - fast_share
```

## Step 3 — Validate

**(a) Compare to vendor UI:** Splunk Search → index=personal | stats count by sourcetype. Totals for the same day/week should match within connector lag (usually one poll interval).

**(b) Field presence:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=evcharger:session earliest=-7d
| head 50
| table _time, fast_share, total_sessions, vin
```

Every column the detection uses should be non-null on recent rows.

**(c) Volume sanity:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=evcharger:session earliest=-30d
| timechart span=1d count
```

Flatlines usually mean a broken token, expired OAuth refresh, or HEC URL change.

**(d) Threshold calibration:** Profile `total_sessions` before alerting:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=evcharger:session earliest=-30d
| stats perc50(total_sessions) AS p50 perc90(total_sessions) AS p90 perc99(total_sessions) AS p99 max(total_sessions) AS hi
```

## Step 4 — Operationalize

Create a companion dashboard titled `UC-25.3.16: Personal evidence` with the following panel layout:

**Panel 1 — Monthly Chart Of Dc Fast-Charge Share (the key fields):** Configure according to standard Splunk visualization patterns for this panel type.


Time picker defaults: set to last 30 days with named presets for 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, and 1y — the auditor needs all five windows without retyping. Enable scheduled PDF export for the full dashboard on the regulation's reporting cadence.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting

**Personal HEC index — no Personal HEC index events / missing fields:** If `evcharger:session` stops updating, re-check HEC token, index `personal`, and firewall to port 8088. Search `index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd group=http_event_collector` for rejection reasons. Confirm the Personal HEC index connector script is still running (`systemctl status` or cron log).

**Personal HEC index — NULL values in extracted fields:** The Personal HEC index JSON export shape drifted — compare a raw event (`index=personal sourcetype=evcharger:session | head 1 | spath`) against the field names in Step 2. Re-map in the connector before changing the SPL.

**Personal HEC index — API error / auth denied (401/403):** Refresh tokens expire on most consumer APIs — re-authorize the scripted input, update `passwords.conf` / env vars, and verify the vendor developer app is not in sandbox mode.

**Personal HEC index — endpoint timeout / HTTP 429 throttling:** Back off the poll interval in the connector; Personal HEC index APIs often cap requests per 15 minutes on free tiers.

**Bucket misalignment:** `span=1m` buckets on UTC by default — if your routine is local-time based, add `| eval _time=_time + (local_offset)` or use `@d` / `@w` snap.

**Stale dashboard:** Confirm the saved search `dispatch.earliest_time` covers enough history for your `1m` buckets.
